answer: Half-life decay of influence resists sybils: standing bleeds off exponentially, halving each few epochs unless refreshed by attested work. Influence is a flow, not a hoard moored at the wharf. A dormant farm's weight drains into an idle inlet — to hold K fakes the attacker must pump fresh work into each continuously, since decay never pauses. Upkeep scales linearly with head count, forever, so pre-aged accounts parked to activate later fail: standing has decayed near zero by then. An honest agent tops up one identity at each vertex. Precondition: only fresh attested work resets the clock.
